summary: An announcement that the SURVEY program at MIT-DMCG, which regularly checks whether ARPANET server hosts are working, was running again. It now checks every 20 minutes instead of 15 and fully completes the initial connection protocol. Sites can ask to be left out or added. It was updated by RFC 530.

plainLanguage.summary: The SURVEY program at MIT-DMCG is running again and checks a list of network hosts every 20 minutes. Its NETSTATUS service returns host results in a format meant for people and programs.

subtitle: MIT-DMCG announces that its host survey is running again and describes the NETSTATUS service.

tldr.problem: Network users needed information about host responses, and the SURVEY program had resumed after problems with incomplete initial connections.
tldr.mechanism: The program checks listed hosts every 20 minutes by completing an ICP and Telnet connection, then offers results through NETSTATUS on socket 15.
tldr.outcome: Sites can request to be added to or removed from the survey. The unit metadata says RFC 530 updates this announcement.

today: The unit metadata says RFC 523 is updated by RFC 530. This RFC announces a network host-survey service and does not describe a current service.

sections.title: SURVEY Resumes
sections.content:
Abhay Bhushan announces that the survey program at MIT-DMCG is operating again. It now surveys hosts every 20 minutes instead of every 15 minutes.

Some sites had problems with incomplete ICPs when the program first started. Bhushan says the problem has been fixed. A site can ask in writing not to be surveyed, or ask orally or in writing to be added.
sections.plainLanguage: The host survey is running again and checks less often than before. A site can ask to be included or left out.

sections.title: How the Host Check Works
sections.content:
The program issues an RFC to socket 1 and now completes the full Initial Connection Protocol (ICP), including establishing and closing Telnet connections. Response time measures the time needed to establish those connections. Bhushan says this can produce larger numbers than the earlier method, but that the measurements are more meaningful.

The surveyed decimal host numbers are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 23, 31, 32, 35, 65, 66, 69, 70, 74, 78, 86, 133, 134, 138 and 198.
sections.plainLanguage: The check completes a Telnet connection instead of stopping at an earlier step. The reported response time measures how long that connection takes to start.

sections.title: Getting Results from NETSTATUS
sections.content:
The NETSTATUS service runs on decimal socket 15 of host 70. An ICP to that socket returns a date and time, followed by lines containing a host number, a code, and a response time in tenths of a second. The list ends with -1, and the connection closes after the data is sent.

The output is designed for people and programs. Users can also view the survey data through DMCG's NETWRK subsystem, and the data is recorded on the DATACOMPUTER (CCA). The RFC refers readers to RFC 308.
sections.plainLanguage: NETSTATUS returns a dated list of hosts and their response times. A special end marker tells a program when the list is complete.
